: She knows.
And it’s because she knows that I must make her forget — a task easier said than done when such powers exist within the hands of God but not my own, despite how godly they may be.
She will be here soon. I can sense it. That foreboding guilt and the mind-numbing sensation of waiting in the confessional after murdering the priest.
Bathed in silence and blood, I assign myself penance while delegating blame to those who helped mold me into the disfigured creature I am today.
I take the Apostles’ Creed and whisper a Hail Mary for each of Our Fathers, hoping the influx of unsanctioned divinity will coat me in a silky-smooth membrane that makes me invisible from above.
It’s the same way I felt in corners in the past in a room that I’ve forgotten but haven’t. And the same thing I hope you feel when you feel the way I feel.
Yet, I feel it’s not enough. And that years if not decades if not centuries of learning that the pen is mightier than the sword mean nothing when I scribe my sins in blood.
But can you read the language I speak? This one I made up. This one where nothing means anything until it happens to you. And then, even when it does, all you see are pretty letters.
Red dresses to match each sentence, or her eyes, or the color of the sky when the reckoning rolls in and you are forced to confront not your demons but mine.
I have brought them here and chained them to pillars of salt. Commanded they consume the corpses I leave at their feet like a cat killing mice for its master.
Alas, I stand here now having not killed one myself, but having scavenged it from a breeding ground. Exactly where it was meant to be. Exactly where the defenses were a little bit thin.
And all I needed to do was look like I belong while donning a pair of pointy ears.
She knows. She knows what I have done.
Yet, remorse does not find me and panic does. Shame. Guilt.
And the incessant desire to drag her into the pit I dug so she can see how much greener the grass can be when all other colors are butchered like lambs.
The bell rings. I sigh. I know my time has come. How the gallows wait impatiently to watch words like “hang” become “hung.”
But in the transition from present to past, where people die but their actions last, perpetuated by others in this collection we’ve amassed, I must ask.
If you were me, and you knew you were wrong, and someone else knew you were wrong, would you tell them you are wrong? Or would you ask why they asked at all?
scene black
I slip deeper down the well.
How much further can I fall?
scene makiconfrontation1
: Uhh...hey.
: Hi. I assume you already know why I’m here. But I brought Sara along for moral support since I felt weird doing this on my own. I hope you don’t mind.
: Is Ami home? I figured I can just hang out with her while you guys talk.
: I think she’s getting ready to go to the mall, but yeah. She’s here. I can’t imagine how much “moral support” you’ll be able to provide from her room, though.
: It was bringing myself to actually, well...bring myself here that was difficult. I can handle the rest on my own, I think.
: Okay...I don’t have a DVD player, though.
scene makiconfrontation2
: Oh, good. Then maybe I can actually get through this without colossally fucking up and making my daughter hate me even more than she already does.
: Kids say a lot of things, Maki. Makoto doesn’t hate you. She’s just a little upset that you...did that really weird thing that you did. I’m sure she’ll get over it soon.
: Which is right when I’m sure I’ll find another way to ruin everything.
: Well, uhh...come in, I guess?
scene black
: Do you guys want, like...coffee or something? Ami got me a book for Christmas about a bunch of different ways to brew it and some sort of wave machine thing.
: What’s “Christmas?” Some kind of religious holiday?
: Oh. Uhh...yeah. Let’s go with that.
scene makiconfrontation3
: Sara! What are you doing here? Are we going camping again?
: Maybe next time, okay? We can still hang out for a little while, though! I’m just moral support today.
: I’m also here. You can say hi to me too.
: Oh, I know. I just don’t like you.
scene makiconfrontation4
: Your daughter’s a real bitch, Akira. Maybe you can give me some advice on how to deal with that?
: Ami, that wasn’t very nice. Apologize to Maki.
: No.
scene makiconfrontation5
: I’m sorry. I’ve done all I can do. Anything else will be overstepping unless Akira marries me and I become Ami’s new mom.
: Ami, go to your room. And take Sara with you.
if amifingered == True:
: Okay. But if the lube dealer lady tries selling you stuff, tell her that you don’t want any because you already have a perfectly good and very reusable toy at home!
else:
: Okay. But if the lube dealer lady tries selling you stuff, remember that you already have a perfectly good and reusable toy at home! You just haven’t ever touched it yet!
scene makiconfrontation6
: Do you really? That’s actually super surprising. I thought most guys just used their hand.
: Did you get it from me? Please tell me it’s not from Amazon. Don’t buy sex toys from Amazon. Shop local, cum local. That’s Bukkake Maki’s slogan.
: Yay! I’m finally part of an adult conversation.
: Ami. Room. Now.
scene makiconfrontation7
: Fiiiiine...Come on, Aunt Sara! You can help me get ready to meet up with my friends.
: Hah...Sorry about that. She can be...unpredictable sometimes.
: Still more effective than me. I’m not sure if I’ve ever successfully gotten Makoto to go to her room before.
scene makiconfrontation8
: Should we sit? So I can talk more about my failures as both a parent and a friend and you can talk about yours as a teacher and authority figure?
: You’re calmer than I expected you to be.
: Yeah, well, I feel like I kind of have to be when everyone has spent the past month gaslighting me into thinking I’m overreacting here.
scene makiconfrontation9
: But let me ask you, Akira. Do you think I’m overreacting? Or do you, as a parent, understand where I’m coming from?
: Because Ami’s a cute girl. Evil, but cute. And I’m sure you’d be extremely protective of her if you started to pick up on signs that she was sleeping with one of your older friends.
: You’re not overreacting at all. You’re right to be worried. It would have been nice not being blindsided by porn, though.
: Yes, I’ve been effectively convinced of that as well. I just figured it would be the easiest way to avoid the song and dance of you never admitting anything. And to that extent, it worked.
: You looked extremely uncomfortable last night. But it was the knowing sort of uncomfortable. Not the kind that stemmed from watching my daughter’s lookalike get fucked on TV.
: So let’s just stop beating around the bush and face the facts. You’re attracted to teenagers. Aren’t you, Akira?
: Being attracted and actually doing something are completely-
: Just answer the fucking question. Are you or are you not attracted to teenagers? Yes or no?
: I can wait here all day.
: ...Fine. Yes. Yes, I am.
scene makiconfrontation10
: Hah...thank God. Not that you’re attracted to teenagers, obviously. Just that I can get you to be honest without a DVD player. I was actually kind of worried about that.
: Maki, I’m not saying it’s fine that I feel this way or anything. But-
: Akira, do you know what Sara said when I told her about what happened?
: No, but I also didn’t even know you told her about what happened until you showed up at my door together.
: When I told her that I thought you were into high schoolers, she said, “Well, duh. He’s a boy.”
: Well...Sara doesn’t exactly come from the most politically correct background...
: When I told her that I thought you might be sleeping with Makoto, she said, “How does Makoto feel about it?”
scene makiconfrontation11
: How does Makoto feel about it? Not, “that’s despicable” or “wow, disgusting.” Just how does she feel?
: Again, your frame of reference here is-
: I went to Haruka as well and her input was somehow even worse. She doesn’t have Sara’s background at all. She had the most average upbringing basically ever.
: Literally no one I know is against this but me. That is weird. And what’s even weirder is that the only other person who seems to even care is the one I’m suspicious of.
: How did this happen? When did everyone become so insane? When did any of this become okay?
: It’s not okay, Maki.
: Then explain it to me. Is it their looks? Their vulnerability? Do you just like that they look up to you? How did this happen?
: It just...did. I don’t think there’s a reason for it.
: At all? Not even what happened to you when you were younger? That didn’t stunt your emotional growth?
: I mean, it almost surely did. But even if none of that stuff ever happened, we can’t guarantee I’d just only be attracted to older women. I don’t get it either. That’s just how it is.
: You kept it from me for so long, though.
: Yeah, well, you have a teenage daughter who you’ve been openly worried about regarding sex for years now. Kind of hard to bear witness to that and then be like, “Damn, she’s hot.”
: I tried, though. I tried telling you that night at the wall that I was way worse than you thought and you just kept telling me it wasn’t my fault. So has your mind just changed or what?
scene makiconfrontation12
: That was before I knew what that meant! You’re my friend! Of course I wasn’t going to assume you were fucking my daughter!
: Is that what Makoto told you then? That we’ve already crossed that line?
scene makiconfrontation13
: ...No. Makoto didn’t admit to anything. She was too busy reminding me that she’d be better off without me.
: And then Miku started going off on some ridiculous made-up tangent about a secret online boyfriend she’s been having sex with and that Makoto was just trying to cover for her.
: So...not really much time to come clean about anything. But either way, I know that if I’m going to hear the truth, it’s going to have to come from you.
: That’s why I asked you directly last night. And why I’ll ask you again now.
: Akira, are you or are you not having sex with my daughter?
scene makiconfrontation14
: Because I already know you’re the “secret online boyfriend.” And I’m hoping you have the balls to come clean about this too.
: Please. Just put me out of my misery.
: Maki, what good will getting an answer even do when you’ve already made up your mind? What will it change?
: Well, for one, it will show me that there’s at least one person out there who respects me.
: Maybe not enough to not fuck my daughter, but enough to be honest. And enough to make me feel like I’m not throwing baseless accusations out into the ether for no reason.
: Then if I say no, what happens?
: I won’t believe you. I just can’t anymore. It has to be you.
: And if I say yes?
: I do one of two things.
: The first is that I go on a long-winded tangent about how this is the greatest betrayal I have ever faced from anyone and that I think you need to be locked away for a very long time.
: I tell you all about how what you’ve been through does not justify or excuse the things you do now and that, as sad as I am for you as a person, I can not and will not support you anymore.
: Your face will make me sick. Every mention of you will make my heart drop. And I will never be able to trust anyone again.
: I’ll be left with no one but two friends who will never understand me and two daughters who will never listen because I’m not worth listening to.
: In several years, I’ll be forced to swallow these feelings and watch as they go off on their own to do more things that will inevitably make me sad.
: I’ll be absolved of watching over them and spared when it comes to failing at exactly that.
: I will never forgive you. And I will ask that you stay away from both of my girls for as long as you live.
: The second...
: Is that I don’t do any of that. And that I sit here while my eyes swell up with tears and my jaw drops as my heart tears into a million tiny pieces.
: I can’t tell you which one will happen either. That’s something we’ll need to find out together.
: Yeah...with all due respect, I think I’d just rather have you not believe me. That sounds way easier for both of us.
: That’s your answer then?...
: That you just...didn’t do anything?...
: Maki, does Makoto know you’re here right now?
: Are you serious? You saw how she acted last night. She’d kill me if she knew I was here.
: Well, unfortunately, I think you came here for nothing. You’re not going to get an answer out of me. You can get one from her if you really need it.
scene makiconfrontation15
: Seriously, Akira?...
: You don’t even have the balls to give it to me straight?...
: I really don’t, actually. I’m kind of pathetic, if you haven’t noticed.
: Forcefully extracting information from me doesn’t work as well as just waiting for me to have an emotional breakdown so I can reveal it on my own. Maybe don’t stop me next time?
scene makiconfrontation16
: Please don’t hurt her...
: This is my daughter, Akira. She deserves at least one adult to look up to.
: Maki, I don’t want to hurt her. Makoto means way more to me than you can probably even comprehend. And if you want to earn her respect, you can’t just go around her like this.
: Do you remember what we talked about the last time we sat here together?...
: Your...husband?
: That’s right...
: And how I needed to step up to make up for him not being around anymore...
: So how did you come out on top?
: Why are you the one she looks up to when you don’t even try?...
: You’re even weaker than me...I don’t understand it.
: I don’t either, Maki. And I know my word doesn’t mean much, if anything, to you at this point, but I am not trying to fill your role. I am not trying to be a parent to her.
: Oh, great. Just a lover then. That’s so much better. Thank you, Akira. I’ll go home now. Sorry for bothering you.
: Hah...I kind of wish you’d just freak out on me. It looked like you were about to for a second.
: I’ve been driven to my knees in the worst way possible. I am desperate and scared and alone and no one will listen to me.
: You’d also have trouble acting in my position. Everything I can do is wrong. There’s no way out.
: There rarely is. It’s all just forward or backwards or around in circles like the ants that we are. Then we die and start over or whatever it is that happens.
: Thanks. That helps too. You’re really good at this.
: No one is going to hurt your daughter, Maki. She’s one of the strongest girls I’ve ever met. And I’m one of the weakest men, so I probably couldn’t even if I tried.
: She might be strong and you might be weak, but I still don’t think you understand the influence you have over these girls, Akira.
: These are the most important years of their lives. Everything you do is going to impact them in ways you can’t even imagine. And I don’t want them ending up on a screen one day.
: So please...stay away from them. There are plenty of other girls out there who aren’t on the verge of being permanently damaged by one wrong move.
: And if they come to me? Should I just ignore them?
: If you can’t keep your hands to yourself, yes. Why is this so hard to understand?
: Because I’m an idiot.
: We’re both idiots — fumbling our way through parenthood with daughters who won’t ever do what we want them to. But at least yours isn’t a fucking psychopath.
: No...just really mean.
scene makiconfrontation17
: Really mean...
: I’ve cried more in the last twenty four hours than I did after Masahiro died...
: I’m at my breaking point, Akira. That’s why all I wanted was a little grace with you. That you’d come clean and just...stop this.
scene makiconfrontation18
: But it seems like you won’t...and now I have to deal with that.
: Well...how will you?
: I don’t know...
: But I’d appreciate it if you’d stay away from my store, my daughter, and me until I can figure that out.
: I really hope you get the help you need.
: Goodbye, Akira.
scene black
: Sniff...Sara? Come on. Let’s go.
: One second! Ami’s almost done with-
: Sara! Let’s go!
: Maki, I’m really sorry. But Makoto will be way better at talking to you about-
: Please, just leave me the fuck alone. Sara!
: Okay, okay. I’m here. Let’s go. Bye, Sensei. Tell Ami she looks cute today! I helped her with her makeup.
: Yeah...I will.
: Bye, guys. Be...safe and whatnot.
: Yeah...be safe.
Maki leaves. Sara leaves. Then later, Ami leaves. And I’m left alone with my thoughts.
But instead of dwelling on them or hating myself for the situation I put a good friend of mine in, I do the exact opposite of what I’m supposed to.
I tap on a name in my phone and wait for someone to answer.
: Hey, Sensei. I was actually meaning to call. Last night-
: Don’t worry about it. Are you free right now? Ami just left.
: Just left...your house? Are you-
: I am.
: I’ll be right over.

There’s something that feels like remorse, but there’s someone to take those feelings away.
Someone I will not be kept from.
Someone you can not hide from me.
